payload.name: Extract explicit emotional reactions as state memories
payload.description: During memory extraction, if a message explicitly says how the person felt about an event, add a state/event memory for the emotion in addition to any plans; do not keep only future-oriented facts.
content: When extracting memories, first scan for explicit emotional reactions (e.g., 'thrilled', 'rewarding', 'felt appreciated') tied to an event.
For each explicit reaction, create a separate 'state' or 'event' memory capturing the feeling and the triggering event, even if the message also contains plans.
Do not omit emotional reactions merely because they are subjective or because a more actionable plan candidate exists in the same message.

solves: When a person explicitly states an emotional reaction (e.g., thrilled, rewarding) to an event, extraction often keeps only the following plans and drops the subjective reaction, making the memory incomplete. This rule ensures those reactions are stored as a state/event memory alongside any plans, so future questions about feelings can be answered.
